test_cases.description: Test that fetch_users returns an array of user objects with only 'name' and 'email' fields when the external API responds with 200 and valid user data.
test_cases.name: Fetch users with successful 200 response

test_setup.given: The JSONPlaceholder API endpoint returns HTTP 200 with a JSON array of user objects, each containing at least 'name' and 'email' fields.
test_setup.then: An array of users is returned, each containing 'name' and 'email'.

test_cases.description: Test that fetch_users returns an empty array when the external API responds with a non-200 HTTP status (e.g., 404).
test_cases.name: Fetch users with non-200 response code

test_setup.given: The JSONPlaceholder API endpoint returns HTTP 404 with an empty body.

test_cases.description: Test that fetch_users returns an empty array and logs an error when a network error (e.g., timeout, connection refused) occurs.
test_cases.name: Fetch users with network error

test_setup.given: A network error occurs during the HTTP GET request to the JSONPlaceholder API.
test_setup.then: An empty array is returned and an error is logged.

test_cases.description: Test that fetch_users returns an empty array and logs an error when the API responds with HTTP 200 but invalid JSON.
test_cases.name: Fetch users with invalid JSON response

test_setup.given: The JSONPlaceholder API endpoint returns HTTP 200, but the response body is not valid JSON.
test_setup.then: An empty array is returned and an error is logged.

test_cases.description: Test that fetch_users returns an empty array when the API responds with HTTP 200 and an empty array.
test_cases.name: Fetch users with empty array response

test_setup.given: The JSONPlaceholder API endpoint returns HTTP 200 with an empty JSON array as the response body.

test_cases.description: Test that fetch_users includes users with missing 'name' or 'email' as null or omits those users, based on implementation, when the API responds with user objects missing these fields.
test_cases.name: Fetch users with missing 'name' or 'email' fields

test_setup.given: The JSONPlaceholder API returns HTTP 200 with a JSON array containing some user objects missing 'name' or 'email' fields.
test_setup.then: Returned array reflects whether users with missing fields are included with nulls or omitted.

test_cases.description: Test that fetch_users returns an empty array if the API responds with HTTP 200 but an empty (not even an array) response body.
test_cases.name: Fetch users with HTTP 200 and empty response body

test_setup.given: The JSONPlaceholder API endpoint returns HTTP 200 with an empty string as the response body.
test_setup.then: An empty array is returned and an error may be logged.

test_cases.description: Verify that the endpoint returns the correct event details and list of users for a valid event ID.
test_cases.name: View event by valid ID

test_setup.given: An event with ID 1 exists and multiple users are present in the system.
test_setup.then: The response contains the event details and a list of all users.
test_setup.when: A GET request is made to /events/1.

test_cases.description: Verify that the endpoint returns an appropriate error when the event ID does not exist.
test_cases.name: View event with nonexistent ID

test_setup.then: The response contains a 404 status and an error message.
test_setup.when: A GET request is made to /events/9999.

test_cases.description: Verify that the endpoint handles requests with invalid event ID formats gracefully.
test_cases.name: View event with invalid ID format

test_setup.given: No event with ID 'abc' exists and the ID format is invalid.
test_setup.then: The response contains a 400 status and an error message.
test_setup.when: A GET request is made to /events/abc.

test_cases.description: Verify that the endpoint returns an empty users array when no users are present in the system.
test_cases.name: View event when no users exist

test_setup.given: An event with ID 2 exists but no users are present in the system.
test_setup.then: The response contains the event details and an empty users array.
test_setup.when: A GET request is made to /events/2.

test_cases.description: Verify that the endpoint returns an error when the event ID is zero, which is typically invalid.
test_cases.name: View event with ID zero

test_setup.then: The response contains a 404 status and an error message.
test_setup.when: A GET request is made to /events/0.

test_cases.description: Verify that the endpoint handles requests for extremely large event IDs gracefully.
test_cases.name: View event with very large ID

test_setup.given: No event with a very large ID exists.
test_setup.then: The response contains a 404 status and an error message.
test_setup.when: A GET request is made to /events/99999999999999.

test_cases.description: Verify that the endpoint still returns a valid response even if the Content-Type header is missing (since it's a GET request with no body).
test_cases.name: View event without Content-Type header

test_setup.given: An event with ID 1 exists and multiple users are present in the system.
test_setup.then: The response contains the event details and a list of all users.
test_setup.when: A GET request is made to /events/1 without the Content-Type header.

test_cases.description: Verify that the endpoint is protected against SQL injection attempts in the event ID parameter.
test_cases.name: View event with SQL injection in ID

test_setup.given: The request contains a SQL injection attempt in the event ID.
test_setup.then: The response contains a 400 status and an error message, and the database is unaffected.
test_setup.when: A GET request is made to /events/1;DROP TABLE users;.
